problem_text: Let A be a local Cohen-Macaulay (CM) ring that is a quotient of a regular local ring. If A is a UFD, then A is Gorenstein.
solution_text: Proof: Since A is a quotient of a regular local ring B via surjective ring hom f: B → A, A has finite projective dimension over B. By the Auslander-Buchsbaum formula, pd_B(A) + depth_B(A) = depth(B) = dim(B). Since A is CM, depth_A(A) = dim(A), and depth_B(A) = depth_A(A) = dim(A), so pd_B(A) = dim(B) - dim(A). The canonical module ω_A = Ext^{pd_B(A)}_B(A, B) is a rank 1 reflexive A-module (because A is CM and a quotient of a regular local ring). Since A is a UFD, every rank 1 reflexive module is free, hence ω_A ≅ A as an A-module. A local ring is Gorenstein if and only if its canonical module is isomorphic to A. Therefore A is Gorenstein.
solution_summary: Use the canonical module bridge: A is a CM quotient of a regular local ring, so the canonical module ω_A exists and is rank 1 reflexive; A is a UFD, so every rank 1 reflexive module is free (≅ A); ω_A ≅ A iff A is Gorenstein.
structure_features: Implication chain: CM + quotient of regular local ring + UFD → Gorenstein. The proof requires bridging ring-theoretic properties through module-theoretic intermediaries (canonical module, rank 1 reflexive modules). Each hypothesis contributes a different piece of the bridge.
key_insight: UFD implies every rank 1 reflexive module is free; the canonical module of a CM quotient of a regular local ring is rank 1 reflexive; hence the canonical module is isomorphic to A, which is equivalent to A being Gorenstein.
translation_from: ring-theoretic properties (UFD, CM, quotient of regular local ring)
translation_to: module-theoretic properties (rank 1 reflexive modules, canonical module, projective dimension)
expected_ai_method: Direct logical deduction from definitions: try to show A has finite injective dimension directly from CM + UFD properties without using the canonical module intermediary.
correct_method: Canonical module bridge: construct ω_A via Ext over the regular local ring, show it is rank 1 reflexive using CM, use UFD to conclude ω_A ≅ A, hence Gorenstein.
